166.t: Joining Nat Cole's band at the Ubangi Club
166.s: He took the bass job at the Ubangi; Nat sang only 'Roses of Picardy' and later offered him a trio job he refused.
166.ch: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
166.q: So we went to a club called the Ubangi, over on Long Beach Boulevard. Exquisite little club. And the chorus line had dwindled down to about four or five. In fact, they had

166.t: Friendship with Nat and Nadine, and the name 'Coles'
166.s: Simmons kept Nat's wife Nadine company; Nat began singing, and they discuss the 'Coles' name and Maria.
166.ch: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
166.q: where as a single. I can't think of where it was. And his wife -- he would leave money with me to take his wife, Nadine, Shorty Nadine, he called her Shorty, wherever she wanted to go, if she wanted to go to the movies or a dance, or wherever. You know, he'd leave money. And the three of us were…

166.t: Gigging in Los Angeles in 1947 and Nat Cole's turn to singing
166.s: Simmons gigged with Happy Johnson and others; Nat Cole refused marijuana to protect his voice and made new records.
166.ch: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
166.q: Oh, I worked with Happy Johnson's Big Band for a while. Different ones off a -- Central Avenue would come up with a gig occassionally. Like the drummers especially, they loved to play with me, you know. After I'd been back - East and been exposed and what not, you know. They all loved me. John…

461.t: Brothers, the songwriting team and recording Nat King Cole
461.s: Rene and brother Otis began songwriting, won a contest with My California Maid, and he recorded Nat King Cole's trio.
461.q: numbers like the you know that was uh standard type of things that you would feature in that type of band at least uh you know which is you know the higher society would be maybe you know uh uh uh Tiger Rag it would be mostly the regular uh uh uh Saints go marching in there would be the standard…

340.t: Nat King Cole as a justified success
340.s: Asked who deserves his record sales, Mancuso picks Nat King Cole, discussing his diction, Hollywood neighbourhood story and foreign-language records.
340.q: No. At one point before he got to California, it was so hard for a black man in the deep south, as you can imagine, he had to whiten up, he thought. Oh it’s scary. There’s a documentary that shows when he was doing it. But when he went out there, and you know, Central Avenue, and all he did with…

86.t: Recording with Art Tatum, Nat King Cole and Sinatra
86.s: He plays with Tatum, recalls an early Nat Cole date at Glen Wallichs' studio and links his success to Basie.
86.ch: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
86.q: I found a few notes but I was so busy listening to Art, all I could do was play the melody. Oh, what a monster he was, oh man. They’re still trying to figure out the things that he was playing back in those days, they haven’t figured it out yet. But as I said before, my career has been just…

225.t: Hearing the Nat King Cole Trio at the Three Sixes
225.s: The band heard the Cole trio before they were famous and were astonished by the arrangements and Nat's piano.
225.q: How about that. I’ll tell you, I would like to recall this incident that happened while we were at Billy Berg's Swing Club. We heard about a place where a trio was playing that was a mind-blowing experience, to go hear this trio.

380.t: Nat Cole as arranger and the early lean years
380.s: They recall Nat's big band, shared ham hocks and beans, and his trio with Wesley Prince and Oscar Moore.
380.ch: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
380.q: Oh, what was I talking about? I just said that he astounded everybody except Art Tatum. But of course, so many people forgot or never did know what a great musician and pianist Nat Cole was. He also was a great arranger. That's something that people didn't know.

232.t: Nat King Cole, the trio, and singing
232.s: Fields toured with Nat Cole, who told him he too had once said he could not sing; Parker Berry doubted Cole could be a vocalist.
232.ch: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
232.q: So we went to talking and he says I heard a lot, they just went nuts over the Beatles, when they bought that tape of them and everything and it looks like they forgot about everybody, because they just didn't do anything at all.

168.t: A star-studded session and the party where Nat King Cole sang
168.s: At a session with Tatum, Barksdale, Ray Nance and Blanton, and at Mary Wilkinson's Hollywood party, Stewart first heard Nat King Cole sing.
168.ch: Movies and the Los Angeles scene
168.q: Well, it's hard to say. I'm sure that Art Tatum was there. And at this one our guitarist, Everett Barksdale, he was on the scene, and I think Duke Ellington was in town with his band also, and Ray Nance was there, I remember, this particular session. And if I'm not mistaken Jimmy Blanton came in.

170.t: Nat Cole remembering him from Chicago
170.s: Nat Cole recalls Ware from Lips Lower Level in 1953 and shakes his hand after the show.
170.q: We played a TV show and what made me feel so good, Nat Cole was in town and he didn't play, but he was a guest, you know, and this guy was questioning him. We played out two or three tunes and I had played opposite Nat Cole back in '53, down at the old Blue Note. It was called Lips Low Level then…

455.t: A night with Nat King Cole and brother Eddie Cole
455.s: Budd sits in at a Hollywood party with Cole's trio and recalls Nat and Eddie Cole struggling in Chicago.
455.q: That's Earl's great solo, you know. So we wrote -- I wrote all of this stuff, and we were able to make enough money to get out of California. In the meantime we were invited out by Nat King Cole to go hang out with him at a party, he was playing a party for some big people there in Hollywood, and…
